Messages.Author: Mark Lamutt
Messages.Body:
Using the Jyhad text of the card (pool is gained from the meth's blood pools, not the
blood bank), does the meth playing this card choose what order around the table he/she
guesses, or does the guessing proceed around the table in the direction of play?

Is the effect of this card considered simultaneous - i.e. if the meth playing the Prank
guesses correctly three times, do the meths lose their pool at the same time, or in the
order guessed?

If the pool loss is simultaneous, and one or more of the players is ousted, who gets the
victory points and the pool gain? If the pool loss is in the order guessed, then this
question is moot.

Thanks for all the answers guys. I appreciate it.

Mark

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
mdla...@wcc.com (Mark Lamutt) wrote:
> Using the Jyhad text of the card (pool is gained from the meth's blood pools,
not the
> blood bank),

The VTES version has been ruled/errata'ed to operate in the same way.

> does the meth playing this card choose what order around the table he/she
> guesses, or does the guessing proceed around the table in the direction of
play?

She chooses.

> Is the effect of this card considered simultaneous - i.e. if the meth playing
the Prank
> guesses correctly three times, do the meths lose their pool at the same time,
or in the
> order guessed?

Simultaneous.

> If the pool loss is simultaneous, and one or more of the players is ousted,
who gets the
> victory points and the pool gain? If the pool loss is in the order guessed,
then this
> question is moot.

As always in the case of simultaneous oustings, the predator gets the VP
regardless of whether the predator is ousted as well.

If the predator is not ousted, she gets six pool.
